newsitem.title: UK: Ivory cocoa arrivals point to 1.1 mln T crop - GNI.
newsitem.headline: Ivory cocoa arrivals point to 1.1 mln T crop - GNI.

text.p: Broker GNI says that arrivals data now suggests a total Ivorian 1996/97 cocoa harvest of at least 1.1 million tonnes, although it has not yet officially revised its crop outlook.
The estimate would indicate a rise of 150,000 tonnes on GNI's last projection in January.
Lawrence Eagles, GNI's head of research, said on Tuesday strong arrivals data from Ivory Coast was pointing to a larger crop than initially estimated.
"We are looking at a situation where the Ivorian crop looks to be at least around 1.1 million tonnes," Eagles told Reuters.
"I can't deny the arrivals figures. It seems very apparent that we have got another big crop," he added.
Industry sources in Abidjan have put arrivals by March 7 at around 920,000-960,000 tonnes, which is already within striking distance of last year's record levels.

"Last year's crop you could inflate by saying there was a certain amount of stock carryover. This year you can say there is a certain amount of stock carryover from last year but you have still got a massive crop," said Eagles.
But GNI was not going to revise its global deficit projection of 180,000 tonnes until first quarter cocoa grind figures were released.
The estimate was likely to be trimmed, Eagles said, but the extent of this depended on the consumption growth.
One crucial factor to monitor was the rate of genuine consumption growth last year after taking into account the re-stocking.
"That is why people are going to be looking at second quarter grind figures to get a firm grasp of what consumption is likely to be this year," Eagles said.
Most industry analysts now see a global cocoa deficit of around 100,000 tonnes, with an Ivorian crop of around 1.050-1.070 million tonnes.
But Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said last week the total harvest was likely to be less than one million tonnes.
